title: Motion-graphics arp bed with glide drop-out
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 1,200,000 samples (25.0 s at 30 fps = 750 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 25-second bright motion-graphics bed in C major at 120 BPM (1 beat = 15 frames). Frames 0-60: intro of descending sine blips (C7, G6, E6, C6 on frames 18, 30, 42, 54) with tiny pitch slides, like UI elements landing. Frame 60: full bed: driving 1/8 sine-square arpeggio on Cmaj7 → Am9 → Fmaj7 → G6 (2 beats each), round kick on every beat, soft sub, clap on 2 and 4. Frames 450-525: a pure sine glide rises smoothly from C5 (523 Hz) to C7 (2093 Hz) on an exponential curve while the kick fades out. Frames 525-540: total silence (half a bar). Frame 540: hit and groove returns. Frame 660: switch to an outro: no drums, a gentle tremolo pad on Cmaj9 and sparse high chimes (C7, E7, G7) every half bar; fade to 0 by frame 750. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.

metrics.note: Public out.wav downsampled to 32000 Hz for Workers ≤5 MiB; metrics from 48 kHz master.

notes: Bright C-major motion bed with 1/8 arp, then exponential sine glide C5→C7 into hard silence and groove return with tremolo outro.
